antipatterns: app/Http/Controllers/ShippingQuoteController.php:15-24 – the controller maps errors with try/catch. That works, but UnknownPostcode could render itself (a render() method on the exception) instead of the controller holding the HTTP mapping.

app/Http/Controllers/ShippingQuoteController.php:22 – the shape of the fallback payload is built inside the controller. A small domain helper would be a better home for it, though it is only one line.
app/Services/CarrierClient.php:72-77 – the reportedAuthFailure() helper has a side effect inside a match arm. Report-then-return is harder to see there than an inline `if (401) report($e)`.
strengths: The retry `when` closure only retries ConnectionException and 5xx responses. A 404 or 401 stops at the first call; my probes confirmed this for 503→404, 500→401 and 429.
Time is bounded: 3 attempts × 1.4 s timeout + 2 × 100 ms sleeps comes to 4.4 s, under the 5 s budget. The constants are named and there is one short comment explaining the budget.
The 401 reports the underlying RequestException once and serves the fallback. A malformed 200 or a non-JSON 200 also falls back.

The tests use Http::preventStrayRequests(), Sleep::fake() (so retries are instant), Exceptions::fake() with assertReported and assertReportedCount, named datasets, a check for the leading-zero postcode, and the URL/bearer token in assertSent.
Uses a FormRequest with a typed postcode() accessor, digits:4 plus string (which rejects array input), and an invokable controller.

antipatterns: tests/Feature/ShippingQuoteTest.php:12-18 – there is no Http::preventStrayRequests() and no Sleep::fake(). Retry tests really sleep, so the suite takes about 1.4 s against about 0.24 s for impl-1. In the validation tests, Http::assertNothingSent() passes trivially without a fake, so a stray request would go to the real network.

tests/Feature/ShippingQuoteTest.php:135-141,155-161 – the tests capture reports through hand-rolled ExceptionHandler::reportable() closures. Laravel 11+ provides Exceptions::fake() and assertReported() for this.
app/Actions/QuoteShipping.php – adds an Action layer between the controller and the client. Its only job is to wrap the fallback, which is ceremony for a feature this small.
app/Exceptions/CarrierUnavailable.php:8 – ShouldntReport has no effect here, because the exception is always caught before it can reach the handler.

app/Services/CarrierClient.php:26 – the budget comment sits in the middle of the fluent chain. connectTimeout(1) is added below timeout(1.4), which is redundant because Guzzle's total timeout already includes the connect time.
strengths: The UnknownPostcode exception has its own render() method returning a 422 with a message, and implements ShouldntReport. This is idiomatic exception-to-response mapping, and it keeps the controller to one line.
The retry predicate and timeouts match impl-1. My probes confirmed no retry on 404, 401 or 429, a 503→404 sequence gives 422, and 500→401 reports once and falls back.
The ternary with `throw` as an expression for the malformed-response guard is compact modern PHP.
Includes a direct unit-level test that CarrierClient::quote() returns the plain array of rates, which is part of the class contract the task asked for.

v.rationale: I found no real bugs in either version. Both pass their own suites (22 tests each), and my probes behaved the same way on both: 503 then 404 gives 422 after 2 calls, a 429 falls back without a retry, a non-JSON 200 falls back, a 404 is not reported, 500 then 401 reports once, and there are exactly 2 sleeps on 5xx. One probe failed on both (fallback_cents as a string): it set a string in config directly, while config/services.php casts the env value to int, so neither has a real defect. Both use the same core Http::retry design with a predicate limited to connection errors and 5xx, and the same 4.4 s worst-case budget. impl-1 ranks higher on the tests and on simplicity. Its tests use preventStrayRequests, Sleep::fake and Exceptions::fake, the modern testing tools for this focus area. impl-2's tests sleep for real, do not prevent stray requests, and capture reports with a hand-rolled reportable() hook. impl-2 also adds an Action class with little purpose. Its best point is the exception that renders its own response, which beats impl-1's try/catch in the controller, but that does not outweigh the weaker tests and the extra layer.
